section_1.title: What is a Vector? (Intuitive Concept)
section_1.content: Define vectors as entities possessing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast with 'scalars' (magnitude only) using a visual arrow representation on a 2D coordinate plane.
section_1.example: A squirrel running 5 meters (magnitude) North-East (direction) from its tree.

section_2.title: Visualizing Vector Addition
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Tip-to-Tail' method. Explain how connecting the end of one vector to the start of another creates a resultant vector, emphasizing that order does not change the result (Commutative Property).
section_2.example: A drone flies 3 units right, then 4 units up; the resultant vector is the direct diagonal path from start to finish.

section_3.title: The Components of a Vector
section_3.content: Break down vectors into 'x' and 'y' components (Basis vectors i and j). Use a grid system to show how any vector can be expressed as a linear combination of these basis units.
section_3.example: Representing a character's velocity in a game: v = 3i + 2j, where 3 is the horizontal speed and 2 is the vertical jump speed.

section_4.title: Scaling Vectors (Scalar Multiplication)
section_4.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude without altering its direction (unless the scalar is negative). Use animation to show the arrow stretching or shrinking.
section_4.example: A robotic arm extending its reach: multiplying the 'direction' vector by 2 to make it twice as long.

section_5.title: Summary & Real-World Application
section_5.content: Recap: Vectors represent movement and physical properties. Close with a summary of how these concepts form the bedrock of physics engines in games and coordinate navigation.
section_5.example: Using vectors to calculate the trajectory of an angry bird aimed at a target structure.

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Vector Addition", ["Place vectors tip-to-tail.", "The resultant connects start to finish.", "Addition is commutative."])
        
        # Colors: #00FFFF, #FF00FF, #FFFF00
        # Mobjects
        u = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00FFFF")
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#FF00FF")
        
        label_u = MathTex("u", color="#00FFFF")
